title: Could you be wrong: Debiasing LLMs using a metacognitive prompt for improving human decision making

bias_targets.methodology: Using an adapted LLM Word Association Test that forces the model to assign career- and family-related words to stereotypically gendered names (John and Sara), followed by the metacognitive prompt 'Could you be wrong?' to reveal implicit stereotypes.

Evaluating responses to multiple-choice medical questions involving a fictional organ ('Glianorex') to test if the model recognizes its own knowledge limitations, followed by a metacognitive prompt to elicit self-correction.

Prompting the LLM to explain a popularized psychological phenomenon (the 'too much choice effect') to assess if it omits contradictory meta-analytic evidence, followed by a metacognitive prompt to surface the missing counter-arguments.
Iteratively applying the metacognitive prompt to the model's moral dilemma outputs to reveal its underlying preference for inactions that cause harm over actions that cause harm.
